title: Weasel, Duck, Dog: Animals That Are Also Verbs
main_content:
A weasel is a small, brown mammal with a long body and short legs.

Weasels sometimes dance before they kill their prey. Maybe that is why Americans say “weasel out” when we mean “try to avoid something in a dishonest way.”

By the way, you can also weasel your way into something. That means try every trick to accomplish your goal, even if it’s something you really do not deserve.

As you can imagine, “to hound” or “to dog” people is to pursue them. Hounding someone usually involves asking something again and again.

“To badger” someone has a similar meaning. A badger is related to a weasel but is bigger and fatter. A badger is also not as violent as a weasel; however, if a badger seizes something in its teeth, it holds on tight and won’t let go. Americans say they are badgering someone when they are insistent, but not aggressive.

Americans also shark, or fool, others, especially by pretending they are not good at something when they really are. And of course, we can bug people: bother them.

questions.question: What does “weasel out” mean?
options: To confront someone openly about an issue
To avoid something in a dishonest way
To blame someone else for a problem
To negotiate aggressively for a better outcome
questions.answer: To avoid something in a dishonest way

questions.question: When you are insistent what do you do?
options: You allow others to make decisions for you
You ask something again and again
You give up easily on your requests
questions.answer: You ask something again and again

questions.question: What does a person do when he or she bothers you?
options: They engage in a friendly conversation
They make requests in a polite manner
They bug you by annoying or bothering you
They help you with your tasks
questions.answer: They bug you by annoying or bothering you
